correctness.rationale: The claim is conditional on bijectivity, with a nonzero coefficient and odd prime-power q. On the fibers of x↦x^D, D=d(q−1), injectivity forces gcd(r,2(q−1))=1. On the induced permutation of μ_{(q+1)/2}, multiplying the images gives B^D=1 for B=a^{(q+1)/2}−(−1)^{(q+1)/2}≠0. Both B and w=a^{(q+1)/2} belong to μ_{2(q−1)}. If w^q=−w, then B^q=−w−(−1)^{(q+1)/2} equals neither B nor −B, a contradiction in odd characteristic. Thus B lies in the base field. The q+1 cosets of F_q^× have even size, and the common power map occurs an even number of times; only the internal translations contribute signs. Their product in F_q^× is δ^{q(r−1)/2}B², where δ generates F_q^×; the quadratic character gives the stated sign. Zero is fixed. An independent replay using quadratic towers and inversion parity tested 16,064 parameters, with 1,142 even and 990 odd permutations; the per-field totals were 16, 288, 288, 480 and 1,060 for q=3,5,7,11,9, respectively.
residual_risks: The replay is bounded; the proof, not that range, covers all odd prime powers and all allowed exponents.
